start: {perfect_click_color}Welcome to Bitstreamer![/color] I'm the Motherboard, the coordinator of everything that happens on this system. Nice to connect with you!
As our new central processor, you'll be running all the programs around here. Let's begin your training!
Programs send us data in the form of {perfect_click_color}bits[/color]. It is your job to receive them when they arrive at your blinking cursor.
To receive a zero bit press {zero_bit_keybind}.
To receive a one bit press {one_bit_keybind}.
Try not to miss any bits or receive them incorrectly. Now, give it a go!
fail_start: Remember, if you wait too long or click too early you won't receive the bit. Try not to receive the wrong bit either! Let's try this again.
enter_bit: Well done! The more accurately you receive bits, the smoother the program will run and as a reward you will receive more {perfect_click_color}score[/color]. Your score is displayed at the top of the screen.
Sometimes you will need to move down to a new line to receive more bits. I will send you a cue to do this, called an {perfect_click_color}enter bit[/color].
If you miss an enter bit, I'll ensure you still move down the line, but you will not gain score and will lose your combo as a result.
*show_combo:Your {perfect_click_color}combo[/color] is displayed in the bottom right. When you receive bits correctly, your combo will increase.
The program runs best when your combo is high, granting you extra score. If you miss or incorrectly receive any bits it will drop back to zero, so be careful!
With all of that in mind, to receive an enter bit press {enter_bit_keybind}. Try it out!
fail_enter_bit: If it wasn't clear, the {perfect_click_color}arrow pointing down[/color] is the enter bit! It is your cue to move down to the next line. Let's take another shot at it.
back_bit: Excellent! When you start running real programs, you should be aware of its {perfect_click_color}health[/color], displayed in the bottom left. If you make too many errors the program will crash!
Missing or incorrectly receiving bits will {perfect_click_color}damage the program[/color]. Missing my enter bits will not, as they don't affect the program's data.
You can regain health by rebuilding your {perfect_click_color}combo[/color]. Receiving bits more accurately will restore the program faster.

One last thing! I may send you a different cue to switch lines, called a {perfect_click_color}back bit[/color]. It behaves just like the enter bit, but instead of moving down you move back {perfect_click_color}up[/color] a line.
To receive a back bit press {back_bit_keybind}. Don't worry about damaging the program for now, let's practice!
fail_back_bit: Sorry if there was any confusion, the {perfect_click_color}arrow pointing up[/color] is the back bit! It is your cue to move back up to the last line. Let's give it another go.
finish: Great job! This concludes your training as our new central processor. I'm sure you'll make a fine replacement for the last one!
Feel free to change your controls to something more comfortable in {perfect_click_color}settings[/color].
Our user is depending on you, good luck!
